etymology: English: immunity qualified by a condition - the right must have been clearly established before the suit.
effect: Ends a suit against an official before the facts are heard, by asking whether an identical case had already spelled the rule out.
available_to: Any official sued in a personal capacity, and the lawyers whose job is to file the motion.
counter: A state law that removes the defence, or a court that treats the Constitution as clearly established on its own terms.

confused_with.tell: Qualified immunity ends the case before the facts; a consent decree ends it after, with an inspector attached.

senses: The doctrine that shields a public official from damages unless the violated right was clearly established at the time - which means the first person to be wronged usually loses, and the rule is established by losing.

It works because it is a rule about rules. The question is not what happened but whether a previous court had described it precisely enough, so each new fact pattern restarts the clock and the law develops only as fast as the plaintiffs who can afford to lose.
example: *"The video was clear, the policy was clear, and **qualified immunity** turned on whether a 2011 case from another circuit had described the same handcuffs."*
